title: Public Endpoints vs Private Endpoints
description: Compare public and private endpoints to understand the security and networking trade-offs for Azure services.

data.text: By default, most Azure services expose a public endpoint accessible over the internet. Private endpoints add a private IP inside your VNet, giving you a second, secure path to the same service.

cards.title: Public Endpoint
cards.description: Default access over the internet with IP restrictions or firewalls.

cards.title: Private Endpoint
cards.description: Private IP inside your VNet with traffic over Azure backbone.

data.title: Hybrid Approach
data.text: You can use both public and private endpoints for the same service. For example, expose Key Vault privately to your VNet while allowing a third-party vendor to use the public endpoint with IP firewall rules.

data.title: Evaluate Access Methods
data.description: For each scenario, decide whether a public endpoint, private endpoint, or both is appropriate.
steps: A mobile app needs to call a Logic App from anywhere.
A production app in a VNet needs to read from Key Vault.
A partner vendor needs to upload files to your Storage account.
data.expectedOutcome: You can justify why each scenario uses public, private, or both endpoint types.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Public endpoints are simple but expose services to the internet.
Private endpoints remove public exposure and keep traffic on Azure backbone.
You can use both for the same service when needed.
data.takeaway: Default to private endpoints for any sensitive service accessed from a VNet.
